claim: Prophylactic antibiotic treatment is not recommended after a tracheostomy.
evidence: However, patients who become rapidly quadriplegic and ventilator-dependent benefit from tracheostomy earlier. Once tracheostomy is performed, careful tracheal toilet and treatment of pulmonary and urinary tract infections by the use of appropriate antibiotics are required; prophylactic antibiotic treatment is not recommended. With tracheostomy and intensive care, the mortality from the disease can be reduced to approximately 3 percent (Ropper and Kehne; see further on under “Prognosis”).
